articles.title: 'Visa matters are sovereign': MEA responds after 115 foreign speakers denied nod for Congress event
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs (MEA) on Friday defended India's visa decisions, saying these are \"sovereign functions\" of every government.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs (MEA) on Friday defended India's visa decisions, saying these are "sovereign functions" of every government. The response came amid allegations that more than 100 foreign speakers invited to the Congress-organised Bharat Summit in Hyderabad were denied entry into India or had their visas cancelled."I would like to say, and all of you are aware, that visa matters are sovereign functions of any country or any government. So that is what I have to say," MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said during his the bi-weekly media briefing.The MEA's response came amid allegations by Congress leaders that several foreign delegates who had received prior clearance from the ministry were subsequently denied entry into India or had their visas revoked. The opposition has alleged that the decisions were taken following instructions from the Union ministry of home affairs (MHA).The two-day Bharat Summit 2026 is being held in Hyderabad on November 13 and 14, bringing together around 1,000 delegates, policymakers and thinkers from 70 countries. Organised by the Congress and the Telangana government, the summit features discussions on global geopolitics, democracy, climate change, artificial intelligence and progressive politics.The controversy has particularly brought Norwegian journalist Helle Lyng into focus, after she claimed that her Indian visa was cancelled shortly before her scheduled departure for Hyderabad, where she was due to participate in a panel discussion on media and press freedom at the Bharat Summit.In a post on X, Lyng said she had received a visa from the Indian embassy in Norway and was scheduled to travel to Hyderabad on Friday. However, she alleged that her visa was cancelled shortly before she was due to leave for the airport, citing "orders from above" in the ministry of home affairs.Lyng's case has also drawn attention because of her earlier interaction with Prime Minister Narendra Modi during his visit to Oslo in May. The Norwegian journalist had questioned PM Modi on press freedom and his reluctance to take questions from journalists during the visit.Political backlashThe reported visa cancellations have triggered a political row, with opposition leaders questioning the government's decision and alleging that foreign journalists and speakers were being prevented from attending the international gathering.Telangana CM A Revanth Reddy launched a sharp attack on Prime Minister Narendra Modi, accusing him of having a dictatorial mindset over the alleged restrictions on foreign journalists attending the Bharat Summit.In a post on X, Reddy alleged that some journalists were stopped from entering India by the ministry of home Affairs despite having received visas. Questioning the reported action, he said, "Is asking Modi ji a question a crime? It is journalists' responsibility to ask questions. Whether to answer them is up to Modi ji."Defending the summit, Reddy said the Invest Telangana Global Summit 2026 aimed to attract investments and generate employment for skilled and unskilled youth, while showcasing Hyderabad's cultural and technological development to representatives from 70 countries.Congress MP Shashi Tharoor also criticised the reported visa cancellations, describing them as a "disappointing footnote" to the Bharat Summit."It is completely unclear under what provision of law the government has taken such a drastic step," he said, adding that reversing the decision was impossible as the conference was scheduled to conclude the following day.Tharoor further criticised the development, saying, "What a shame that a proud democracy has become so insecure that it must stifle any voices it fears will be critical!"Meanwhile, former foreign secretary Kanwal Sibal took a contrasting position, criticising the Norwegian side over the controversy and calling its conduct "unacceptable".In a post on X, Sibal said, "The Norwegians are being very presumptuous. Trying to put us on the mat."Suggesting a tougher response, he added, "Our answer to this should be to tighten up grant of visas to Norwegian journalists."The BJP, meanwhile, defended the visa cancellations, branding the gathering an "Anti-Bharat Summit" and accusing the Congress of bringing together radical Left and anti-India groups.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.summary: Karnataka’s Bibi Fathima SHG and farmer Eshwaragouda Patil win PPVFRA National Plant Genome Saviour Awards for conserving indigenous seeds and millets.
articles.body: Hubballi: Bibi Fathima Self-Help Group of Theertha village and farmer Eshwaragouda Patil (52) of Mattigatti village in Kundgol taluk received national-level Plant Genome Saviour Awards from Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers’ Rights Authority (PPVFRA).Bibijan M Halemani, leader of Bibi Fathima SHG, and Patil received the awards from PK Mishra, principal secretary to Prime Minister, during PPVFRA’s 22nd Foundation Day celebrations in New Delhi on Thursday.The awards recognise outstanding contributions to conserving indigenous crop varieties, protecting agricultural biodiversity and preserving farmers’ traditional knowledge. The award for the collective carries Rs 10 lakh, a citation and a memento.Halemani said Desi Seed Producers Company Limited, Mysuru, was also selected from Karnataka. Bibi Fathima SHG, a women-led collective, conserves indigenous crop varieties, traditional seeds and local food culture.Patil was among three Karnataka farmers honoured for conserving traditional crop varieties and indigenous seeds. The others were CP Krishna of Gulurdoddi village in Maddur taluk, Mandya district, and Asma Banu of Sanoor village in Karkala taluk, Udupi district. Each received Rs 1 lakh and a citation.Patil began seed conservation in 2015 under Agriculture Department’s Organic Village Programme, supported by Sahaja Samrudha. He helped reintroduce Proso Millet (Baragu) and Brown Top Millet (Korale), which had almost disappeared from North Karnataka. articles.title: In 2023, Harvard put honesty researcher Francesca Gino on leave over claims she faked data, and stripped her tenure in 2025; now a federal judge has thrown out her $25 million lawsuit against the university
articles.summary: A three-year legal battle between Harvard University and former Harvard Business School professor Francesca Gino has ended in a major victory for the
articles.body: A three-year legal battle between Harvard University and former Harvard Business School professor Francesca Gino has ended in a major victory for the university, after a federal judge dismissed all of her remaining claims. The ruling, delivered on November 2, 2026, rejects Gino's allegations that Harvard breached its contractual obligations, discriminated against her because of her gender and retaliated against her during an investigation into research misconduct. The decision was reported by Inside Higher Ed, GBH News and Bloomberg Law. US District Judge Myong J. Joun granted Harvard's request for summary judgment, concluding that the evidence did not provide a reasonable basis for a jury to find that the university had improperly revoked Gino's tenure or violated its established procedures. Gino, a prominent behavioural scientist whose work focused on honesty, ethics, decision-making and workplace behaviour, had sought $25 million in damages through a lawsuit filed in 2023. She had accused Harvard, along with former Harvard Business School dean Srikant Datar and researchers associated with the blog Data Colada, of wrongdoing in connection with the allegations against her. The latest ruling disposes of all her remaining claims against Harvard and Datar. However, a separate defamation counterclaim brought by the university against Gino remains unresolved.How the research controversy beganThe controversy dates back to 2021, when three behavioural scientists behind Data Colada, an academic blog examining research integrity, raised allegations of data manipulation in studies co-authored by Gino. The researchers identified irregularities in several published papers, including work examining whether signing an honesty declaration before completing a form could make people less likely to lie. Their findings raised questions about the reliability of data used in Gino's research.Harvard subsequently launched an investigation into the allegations. In June 2023, the university placed Gino on administrative leave while its inquiry continued. She denied the accusations and challenged the way the investigation was conducted. Following a lengthy internal review, Harvard's governing corporation voted in May 2025 to revoke her tenure and terminate her appointment. The decision was particularly significant because removing a tenured professor is an exceptionally rare step at the university.Why the judge rejected her claimsGino's lawsuit argued that Harvard had departed from its own academic policies, failed to follow appropriate disciplinary procedures and used the research misconduct allegations as a pretext for discriminatory treatment. However, Judge Joun found that the university had a sufficient evidentiary basis for its decision and that the record did not establish that Harvard had acted dishonestly or improperly in handling the tenure proceedings.He also rejected her argument that the university's actions reflected gender discrimination, finding insufficient evidence of a broader pattern of discriminatory treatment that could support her allegations. The judge's decision focused on whether Harvard had followed its contractual obligations and reached its decision through a reasonable process. It was not an independent scientific determination of whether Gino had fabricated research data. She has consistently denied research misconduct.Harvard's counterclaim remains openAlthough the ruling ends Gino's claims against the university and Datar, the legal dispute is not entirely over. Harvard has a separate defamation counterclaim against her, accusing her of damaging the university's reputation. It has also alleged that she supplied investigators with a falsified dataset, an allegation she disputes.The university filed a motion for sanctions in September 2026, accusing Gino of concealing or destroying evidence. Judge Joun said that issue would be addressed separately, with further proceedings and an evidentiary hearing.For now, the summary judgment marks a decisive setback for Gino, whose challenge had sought to overturn one of the most consequential disciplinary decisions in Harvard's recent academic history. Whether she will appeal the latest ruling remains unclear.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.summary: Jalgaon DCC Bank polls heat up as Sumit Patil’s rejected nomination is restored, ending BJP-backed unopposed bid in Pachora; alliance seat-sharing row grows.
articles.body: Nashik: Rejection, and subsequent restoration, of Sumit Patil’s nomination has become the central flashpoint in the Jalgaon District Central Cooperative Bank election, scheduled for Nov 29.The decision has ended the prospect of an unopposed victory for BJP-backed candidate Satish Shinde in Pachora and sharpened tensions within the ruling Mahayuti alliance. Sumit is the son of Pachora Shiv Sena MLA Kishor Patil.A senior Shiv Sena functionary said that with Sumit back in the fray, the key BJP-backed candidate Satish Shinde’s prospects of an unopposed victory from Pachora have now been dashed.The Mahayuti alliance aims to contest unitedly, but seat-sharing friction has stalled a final agreement. At a meeting in Jalgaon attended by Girish Mahajan, Gulabrao Patil and NCP leaders, BJP demanded the largest share of nine seats. The deadlock continues over Muktainagar, Bhadgaon, Raver and Chopda, compounded by Kishor Patil’s absence from the meeting.The crisis began on Nov 3 when returning officer Manoj Chaudhary disqualified Sumit, prompting Kishor Patil to state that there are invisible forces working against his family.Sumit challenged the rejection before the divisional joint registrar of cooperatives in Nashik. The appellate authority overturned the returning officer’s order and declared his nomination valid, allowing him to re-enter the electoral contestWith over 300 candidates in the fray and none withdrawing, the contest intensified for the 21-member board of directors for the 2026-2031 term, comprising 15 taluka representatives and six reserved seats.Over 3,000 eligible voters make up the electoral roll. Heavyweights including Union minister Raksha Khadse, ministers Girish Mahajan and Gulabrao Patil, and MLA Mangesh Chavan entered the fray.A senior BJP member said the development underscored how North Maharashtra’s cooperative sector was losing its traditional grassroots ethos to aggressive party politics. articles.title: British children's author David Walliams investigated over grooming, assault allegations involving minors
articles.summary: British comedian and children’s author David Walliams is being investigated by London police over a series of alleged sexual offences.
articles.body: British comedian and children’s author David Walliams is being investigated by London police over a series of alleged sexual offences. The investigation follows reports by leading British media houses stating that he used his celebrity status to groom teenage girls and young women.The Metropolitan Police said on Friday that it had received several allegations of non-recent sexual offences in recent days. The force stressed that the complaints under investigation are separate from those detailed in a joint investigation by ITV News and The Guardian, but said officers would examine the media reports to establish whether they contained evidence of further offences.The allegations reported by the two outlets include claims that Walliams sexually assaulted a woman at his London home when she was 15 and groomed other girls while they were teenagers. The three-year investigation involved speaking to more than 100 people, the outlets said.Walliams, 55, has denied the allegations, insisting he had not broken the law and was not a sexual predator. In a written response to ITV News and The Guardian, he said he was “devastated” that women he had met 10 to 20 years ago had expressed hurt or anger towards him.“Whilst a power imbalance is inevitable when one party is famous, abusing that power is something else entirely and it is something that I never did,” he said.Detective Superintendent Mike Cagney, who is leading the investigation, urged anyone who had experienced a sexual offence to contact police, regardless of when it occurred. He said specialist officers were available to support complainants.The investigation follows Walliams’ unsuccessful attempt to obtain a court injunction preventing The Guardian and ITV News from publishing their findings. His lawyers argued that publication could lead him to take his own life, citing two previous suicide attempts. A medical expert appointed jointly by both sides found that publication posed a serious risk to his mental health.However, High Court judge Mr Justice Nicklin rejected the injunction, ruling that blocking the reports would be an “exceptionally serious interference” with the media’s freedom of expression. The court was not deciding whether the allegations against Walliams were true, but whether the reporting could be legally prevented.The controversy has already had consequences for the entertainer’s career. Publisher HarperCollins dropped him last year following allegations of inappropriate behaviour, while his literary agency also severed ties with him. The BBC has begun removing some of his programmes, including Little Britain, from iPlayer, and his Labour Party membership has been suspended.Walliams, best known for co-creating and starring in the comedy series Little Britain, is also one of Britain’s best-selling children’s authors.You use AI every day.
